He remained here eight years, but not without visiting, at later, walk different cities of Italy, either on the affairs of his order, or for pleasure, or for health. In 1755, he undertook a longer journey, reversed a part of Germany, proceeded as far as Strauburg and Nancy, and removed by way of Germany into Italy, taking with him two younger princes, sons to nephew of the Prince of Holeniee, who had requested him to take charge of their education. He made the year following another journey into France, along with the oldest of these two young Princes, and lodged, while at Paris, at the College of Auswäcrand. It was during this excursion that he wrote the famous _Leices of Virgil_, which were published at Venice with his sister, verses, and those if Poynt and Algarro.
